summary: LiF films were deposited using LiN(SiMe3)2 as a precursor and SF6 plasma as a coreactant. The process yielded conformal, polycrystalline films with a growth rate of approximately 0.4 Å per cycle. The films were slightly lithium-rich with a composition of LiF0.8 and showed low impurity levels. The study highlights the advantages of using SF6 plasma as a fluorine source for ALD of LiF, offering a safer alternative to traditional coreactants like HF.
evidence: Lithium fluoride films were prepared by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using a new route in which LiN(SiMe3)2 is used as a precursor and SF6 plasma as a coreactant. Conformal LiF films were deposited at 150 1C at a growth rate of B0.4 Å per cycle. All deposited films were polycrystalline and slightly lithium-rich with a composition of LiF0.8, independently of the plasma conditions. The use of SF6 plasma as a fluorine source is highlighted as a promising alternative to other coreactants for ALD of high purity lithium fluoride.
